title: Transportation Safety Plan
description: Free Transportation Safety Plan template you can edit online and download as PDF. Covers fleet information, 1.0 driver qualification & training, 2.0 vehicle maintenance & inspection.

2.0 Vehicle Maintenance & Inspection

2.1 PRE-TRIP INSPECTION CHECKLIST:

☐ Brakes (air/hydraulic) - Tested and functional

☐ Tires - Proper inflation, no damage, sufficient tread

☐ Lights - Headlights, taillights, turn signals, reflectors

☐ Steering - No excessive play, smooth operation

☐ Suspension - No broken springs, shocks, or mounts

☐ Windshield & Wipers - No cracks, wipers functional

☐ Mirrors - Clean, properly adjusted

☐ Horn - Working

☐ Emergency Equipment - Fire extinguisher, triangles, flares

☐ Cargo - Properly loaded and secured

☐ Coupling - Fifth wheel, glad hands, electrical connections

☐ Fluid Levels - Oil, coolant, fuel, DEF

2.2 MAINTENANCE PROGRAM:

☐ Maintenance Facility: ______________

3.0 Hours Of Service Compliance

3.1 PROPERTY-CARRYING DRIVERS (49 CFR 395.3):

☐ 14-Hour Limit: Cannot drive after 14 hours on-duty

☐ 11-Hour Limit: Maximum 11 hours driving after 10 hours off-duty

☐ 60/70-Hour Limit: 60 hours in 7 days OR 70 hours in 8 days

☐ 30-Minute Break: Required after 8 hours of driving

3.2 PASSENGER-CARRYING DRIVERS (49 CFR 395.5):

☐ 15-Hour Limit: Cannot drive after 15 hours on-duty

☐ 10-Hour Limit: Maximum 10 hours driving after 8 hours off-duty

☐ 60/70-Hour Limit: 60 hours in 7 days OR 70 hours in 8 days

4.0 Drug & Alcohol Testing Program

4.1 TESTING TYPES:

☐ PRE-EMPLOYMENT: Required before first safety-sensitive function

☐ RANDOM: Minimum 50% annual testing rate for drugs, 10% for alcohol

☐ POST-ACCIDENT: Required for qualifying accidents

☐ REASONABLE SUSPICION: Based on trained supervisor observations

☐ RETURN-TO-DUTY: After positive test/violation

☐ FOLLOW-UP: Unannounced testing after return-to-duty

5.0 Cargo Securement

5.1 SECUREMENT DEVICE REQUIREMENTS:

☐ Tiedowns: Minimum of 2 for all cargo

☐ Working Load Limit (WLL): Must be marked on all devices

☐ Aggregate WLL: Must equal at least 50% of cargo weight

☐ Edge Protection: Required where tiedowns contact sharp edges

5.2 SPECIFIC CARGO REQUIREMENTS:

CARGO TYPE

Roll-on/Roll-off Heavy Equipment Logs Metal Coils Concrete Pipe Hazardous Materials2 tiedowns per unit 4 tiedowns if > 10,000 lb Specialized equipment Cradles, chocks Chocks, wedges Additional requirementsRearmost tiedown within 10 ft Manufacturer tie-down points Chains with hooks, proper load distribution Prevent forward and lateral movement Prevent rolling Placarding, segregation

7.0 Accident & Incident Response

7.1 ACCIDENT PROCEDURES:

STEP 1: Ensure safety - Check for injuries, protect scene

STEP 2: Call 911 if injuries or hazardous materials

STEP 3: Notify Safety Department: ______________

STEP 4: Exchange information with other parties

STEP 5: Document scene (photos, witness statements)

STEP 6: Complete accident report within 24 hours

STEP 7: Submit report to insurance carrier

7.2 ACCIDENT REPORTING FORMS:

☐ Motor Vehicle Accident Report (MCS-50) - Required within 30 days

☐ Post-Accident Drug & Alcohol Testing - Within 32 hours

☐ Insurance Claim Report - Immediately

7.3 CRITICAL INCIDENT RESPONSE:

☐ Fatality - Immediate notification to FMCSA (1-800-832-5660)

☐ Hazardous Materials Release - Notification to NRC (1-800-424-8802)

☐ Major Property Damage - Notification to insurance carrier
